title: Heading After a Top Box Line

illustrates.quote: Do not insert a blank line between the top line of a box and a heading that immediately follows.

blocks.features: Centered, bold blue serif, first line inside a boxed callout with a torn-paper-style top/bottom border.

blocks.text: **Sit upright and lean forward.** By remaining upright, you reduce blood pressure in the veins of your nose.
blocks.features: Bold lead-in phrase ('Sit upright and lean forward.') followed by plain body text, inside the same box.

print.notes: Illustrates no blank line between the box's top rule and the heading that immediately follows it, per rule 4.3.5.
print.printFeatures: Boxed callout with a torn-paper-style top and bottom border; heading centered in bold blue immediately below the top border, body paragraph below that with a bold lead-in phrase.

braille.notes: Line 1 blank; line 2 the top box line (40 dot-7 cells); line 3 the centered heading directly beneath with no blank line, per 4.3.5; line 4 blank; lines 5-6 the paragraph, its bold lead-in phrase wrapped in an emphasis indicator pair, ending in the '444' continuation marker; line 7 the bottom box line; line 8 blank.

uncertain: This paragraph directly follows the heading with no blank line (per 4.3.5); Emboss's formatPara still applies its ordinary 2-cell first-line indent rather than starting flush at column 1 as the gold braille does -- see standards-findings.md F-39. Expect a documented mismatch limited to this indent (and consequent re-wrapping), not a content bug.
resolution: braille.lines agree; only prose wording differed (merged). Heading confirmed centered (level 1) by the centering-formula check. During model-building verification, the paragraph's bold lead-in phrase needed **markup** in print.blocks (it had been described in `features` but never actually marked in `text`); with that fix, this file's only remaining difference from the real Emboss output is the systematic heading-then-paragraph flush-indent gap recorded as standards-findings.md F-39.
